questions.questionText: A car travels the first third of a distance with a speed of $10 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$, the second third with a speed of $20 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$, and the last third with a speed of $60 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$. The average speed of the car for the whole journey is:

solutions.newText:
Let the total distance be $3 x$. The time taken for each part is $ t_{1}=\frac{x}{10}, t_{2}=\frac{x}{20}$, and $t_{3}=\frac{x}{60}$. The average speed is the total distance divided by the total time.
$$
\begin{gathered}
v_{a v g}=\frac{\text { Total Distance }}{\text { Total Time }}=\frac{3 x}{t_{1}+t_{2}+t_{3}}=\frac{3 x}{\frac{x}{10}+\frac{x}{20}+\frac{x}{60}} \\
v_{a v g}=\frac{3}{\frac{6+3+1}{60}}=\frac{3 \times 60}{10}=18 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}
\end{gathered}
$$

questions.questionText: A particle moves along a straight line such that its displacement $x$ at any time $t$ is given by $x=\left(t^{3}-6 t^{2}+3 t+4\right)$ meters. The velocity when the acceleration is zero is:

solutions.newText:
Velocity ( $v$ ) and acceleration ( $a$ ) are found by differentiating displacement ( $x$ ).
$$
v=\frac{d x}{d t}=3 t^{2}-12 t+3
$$
$$
a=\frac{d v}{d t}=6 t-12
$$
Set acceleration to zero: $6 t-12=0 \Longrightarrow t=2 s$. Substitute this time into the velocity equation:
$$
v(t=2)=3(2)^{2}-12(2)+3=12-24+3=-9 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
$$

questions.questionText: The position of a particle is given by $\vec{r}=\left(3 t \hat{i}-2 t^{2} \hat{j}+4 \hat{k}\right) \mathrm{m}$ where $t$ is in seconds. The magnitude of the velocity of the particle at $t=2 \mathrm{~s}$ is:

solutions.newText:
The velocity vector $\vec{v}$ is the derivative of the position vector $\vec{r}$.
$$
\vec{v}=\frac{d \vec{r}}{d t}=3 \hat{i}-4 t \hat{j}
$$
At $t=2 \mathrm{~s}$, the velocity vector is: $\vec{v}(t=2)=3 \hat{i}-4(2) \hat{j}=3 \hat{i}-8 \hat{j}$.
The magnitude is: $|\vec{v}|=\sqrt{(3)^{2}+(-8)^{2}}=\sqrt{9+64}=\sqrt{73} \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$.

questions.questionText: A body starting from rest moves with uniform acceleration. The ratio of the distance covered in the 4 th second to the distance covered in the 3rd second is:
topics: Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion

solutions.newText:
Distance covered in the $n^{\text {th }}$ second ( $u=0$ ) is $S_{n}=\frac{a}{2}(2 n-1)$.
$$
\frac{S_{4}}{S_{3}}=\frac{\frac{a}{2}(2(4)-1)}{\frac{a}{2}(2(3)-1)}=\frac{7}{5}
$$

analysisTags: Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion

questions.questionText: The relation between time $t$ and distance $x$ is $t=a x^{2}+b x$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants. The acceleration is:

solutions.newText:
Differentiate $t=a x^{2}+b x$ with respect to $t$ :
$$
1=2 a x \frac{d x}{d t}+b \frac{d x}{d t} \Longrightarrow 1=v(2 a x+b) \Longrightarrow v=\frac{1}{2 a x+b}
$$
Differentiate $v$ with respect to $t$ to find acceleration:
$$
a_{a c c}=\frac{d v}{d t}=\frac{-1}{(2 a x+b)^{2}} \cdot\left(2 a \frac{d x}{d t}\right)=-(2 a v) \cdot v^{2}=-2 a v^{3}
$$

questions.questionText: A ball is thrown vertically upward. It has a speed of $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ when it has reached one-half of its maximum height. What is the maximum height reached? (Use $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$ )

solutions.newText:
Let max height be $H$. At $H$, final velocity is $0.0^{2}=u^{2}-2 g H \Longrightarrow u^{2}=2 g H$. At $H / 2$, speed is $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} .10^{2}=u^{2}-2 g(H / 2) \Longrightarrow 100=u^{2}-g H$.
Substituting $u^{2}: 100=2 g H-g H= g H \Longrightarrow H=100 / 10=10 \mathrm{~m}$.

questions.questionText: Refer to the figure. What is the ratio of speed in the first two seconds to the speed in the next four seconds?

solutions.newText:
Speed is the magnitude of the slope of the displacement-time (S-t) graph.
- Speed in the first 2 seconds $\left(v_{1}\right)$ : The graph is a line from $(0,0)$ to $(2, \mathrm{~s})$.
$$
v_{1}=\frac{\Delta S}{\Delta t}=\frac{s-0}{2-0}=\frac{s}{2}
$$
- Speed in the next 4 seconds $\left(v_{2}\right)$ : The graph is a line from $(2, \mathrm{~s})$ to $(6,0)$. The time interval is from $\mathrm{t}=2 \mathrm{~s}$ to $\mathrm{t}=6 \mathrm{~s}$.
$$
\text { velocity }=\frac{\Delta S}{\Delta t}=\frac{0-s}{6-2}=-\frac{s}{4}
$$
Speed is the magnitude of velocity, so $v_{2}=\left|-\frac{s}{4}\right|=\frac{s}{4}$.
section*{- Ratio of speeds:}
$$
\frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}}=\frac{s / 2}{s / 4}=\frac{s}{2} \times \frac{4}{s}=\frac{4}{2}=2
$$
The ratio $v_{1}: v_{2}$ is $2: 1$.

questions.questionText: A train moving at $30 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ reduces its speed to $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ while covering a distance of 100 m . If the retardation is constant, how much further will it travel before coming to rest?
topics: Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion

solutions.newText:
First, find acceleration $a: 10^{2}=30^{2}+2 a(100) \Longrightarrow 100=900+200 a \Longrightarrow a=-4 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$. Now, find the further distance $s^{\prime}$ from $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ to rest ( $v=0$ ):
$$
0^{2}=10^{2}+2(-4) s^{\prime} \Longrightarrow 8 s^{\prime}=100 \Longrightarrow s^{\prime}=12.5 \mathrm{~m}
$$

analysisTags: Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion

questions.questionText: The displacement $x$ of a particle varies with time $t$ as $x=a e^{-\alpha t}+b e^{\beta t}$, where $a, b, \alpha, \beta$ are positive constants. The velocity of the particle will: [Given (  $b{\beta} > a{\alpha}$ ) ]

solutions.newText: $v=\frac{d x}{d t}=-a \alpha e^{-\alpha t}+b \beta e^{\beta t}$. As $t$ increases, the first term ( $e^{-\alpha t}$ ) approaches zero while the second term ( $e^{\beta t}$ ) increases exponentially. Thus, the velocity will increase with time.

questions.questionText: A particle moves in a straight line with a constant acceleration. It changes its velocity from $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ to $20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ while passing through a distance of 135 m in $t$ seconds. The value of $t$ is:

solutions.newText:
Using $s=\left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right) t$ :
$$
135=\left(\frac{10+20}{2}\right) t \Longrightarrow 135=15 t \Longrightarrow t=9 \mathrm{~s}
$$

questions.questionText: A particle is moving such that its position coordinate ( $x$ ) varies with time ( $t$ ) as $x=2 t-5 t^{2}$. The average velocity of the particle in the time interval 0 to 2 seconds is:
A train moves from one station to another in 2 hours time. Its speed-time graph during this motion is shown in the figure. The maximum acceleration during the journey is
topics: Graphs of motion in a straight line

solutions.newText:
Acceleration is the slope of the speed-time graph. We need to find the steepest positive slope.
- Segment AB ( $\mathbf{t}=\mathbf{0}$ to $\mathbf{0 . 7 5 h}$ ): $a_{A B}=\frac{20-0}{0.75-0}=\frac{20}{3 / 4} \approx 26.67 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~h}^{-2}$.
- Segment BC ( $\mathbf{t}=\mathbf{0 . 7 5}$ to $\mathbf{1 . 0 0 h}$ ): The speed is constant, so the slope is $a_{B C}=0$.
- Segment CD ( $\mathbf{t}=\mathbf{1 . 0 0}$ to 1.25h): The speed increases from 20 to $60 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$.
$$
a_{C D}=\frac{60-20}{1.25-1.00}=\frac{40}{0.25}=160 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~h}^{-2}
$$
- Segment DE ( $\mathbf{t}=\mathbf{1 . 2 5}$ to $\mathbf{2 . 0 0 h}$ ): The speed decreases (deceleration). The slope is negative.
The maximum acceleration occurs during the interval CD and is $160 \mathrm{~km} \mathrm{~h}^{-2}$.

analysisTags: Graphs of motion in a straight line

questions.questionText: Two cars A and B are moving in the same direction with velocities $30 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and $20 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. When car A is at a distance $d$ behind car B, the driver of car A applies the brake producing a uniform retardation of $2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$. There will be no collision when:

solutions.newText: Relative velocity $u_{\text {rel }}=30-20=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. Relative acceleration $a_{\text {rel }}=-2-0=-2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$. For no collision, the relative separation covered before relative velocity becomes zero must be less than $d . v_{\text {rel }}^{2}=u_{\text {rel }}^{2}+2 a_{\text {rel }} s_{\text {rel }} \Longrightarrow 0^{2}=10^{2}+2(-2) s_{\text {rel }} \Longrightarrow s_{\text {rel }}=25 \mathrm{~m}$. Thus, for no collision, the initial separation must be $d>25 \mathrm{~m}$.

questions.questionText: The velocity of a particle is $v=v_{0}+g t+f t^{2}$. If its position is $x=0$ at $t=0$, then its displacement after unit time ( $t=1$ ) is:

solutions.newText: $x=\int v d t=\int\left(v_{0}+g t+f t^{2}\right) d t=v_{0} t+\frac{1}{2} g t^{2}+\frac{1}{3} f t^{3}+C$. Given $x(0)=0 \Longrightarrow C=0$. At $t=1$, $x(1)=v_{0}(1)+\frac{g}{2}(1)^{2}+\frac{f}{3}(1)^{3}=v_{0}+g / 2+f / 3$.

questions.questionText: A body travels for 15 seconds starting from rest with constant acceleration. If it travels distances $S_{1}, S_{2}$, and $S_{3}$ in the first five seconds, second five seconds and next five seconds respectively, the relation between $S_{1}, S_{2}$, and $S_{3}$ is:

solutions.newText: The ratio of distances covered in successive equal time intervals is $1: 3: 5$. Thus, $S_{1}: S_{2}: S_{3}= 1: 3: 5$, which means $S_{1}=S_{2} / 3=S_{3} / 5$.

questions.questionText: The velocity $v$ versus $t$ graph of a body in a straight line is as shown in figure The displacement of the body in 5 sec is
topics: Graphs of motion in a straight line

solutions.newText:
Displacement is the net area under the velocity-time graph.
- Area $1(\mathbf{t}=\mathbf{0}$ to $\mathbf{3 s})$ : Triangle above the axis. Base $=3 \mathrm{~s}$, Height $=2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$.
$$
A_{1}=\frac{1}{2} \times \text { base } \times \text { height }=\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 2=3 \mathrm{~m}
$$
- Area 2 ( $\mathbf{t}=\mathbf{3}$ to $\mathbf{4 s}$ ): Triangle below the axis. Base $=1 \mathrm{~s}$, Height $=-2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$.
$$
A_{2}=\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times(-2)=-1 \mathrm{~m}
$$
- Area $3(t=4$ to 5 s$)$ : Rectangle above the axis. Base $=1 \mathrm{~s}$, Height $=1 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$.
$$
A_{3}=1 \times 1=1 \mathrm{~m}
$$
Total displacement $\Delta x=A_{1}+A_{2}+A_{3}=3+(-1)+1=3 \mathrm{~m}$.

analysisTags: Graphs of motion in a straight line

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the displacement-time graph for a particle moving in a straight line. The average velocity for the interval $t=0$ to $t=5$ is
topics: Graphs of motion in a straight line

solutions.newText:
Average velocity is defined as total displacement divided by total time.
$$
v_{\text {avg }}=\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}=\frac{x_{\text {final }}-x_{\text {initial }}}{t_{\text {final }}-t_{\text {initial }}}
$$
From the graph:
- Initial position at $t=0$ is $x_{\text {initial }}=0 \mathrm{~m}$.
- Final position at $t=5$ is $x_{\text {final }}=-10 \mathrm{~m}$.
- The time interval is $\Delta t=5-0=5 \mathrm{~s}$.
$$
v_{a v g}=\frac{-10-0}{5-0}=\frac{-10}{5}=-2 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
$$

analysisTags: Graphs of motion in a straight line

questions.questionText: The motion of a particle is described by the equation $x=a+b t^{2}$ where $a=15 \mathrm{~cm}$ and $b=3 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$. Its instantaneous velocity at time $t=3 \mathrm{~s}$ will be:

solutions.newText: $v=\frac{d x}{d t}=2 b t$. At $t=3 s, v=2(3)(3)=18 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$.

questions.questionText: If a car at rest accelerates uniformly to a speed of $144 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ in 20 s , it covers a distance of:

solutions.newText: $v=144 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h} \times \frac{5}{18}=40 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} . u=0 . s=\left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right) t=\left(\frac{0+40}{2}\right) \times 20=400 \mathrm{~m}$.

questions.questionText: A particle moves along a path such that its displacement is given by $x^{2}=t^{2}+1$. Its acceleration is given by:

solutions.newText: Differentiating $x^{2}=t^{2}+1$ w.r.t. time: $2 x \frac{d x}{d t}=2 t \Longrightarrow x v=t$. Differentiating again: $v \cdot v+x \cdot a=1 \Longrightarrow v^{2}+x a=1$. $a=\frac{1-v^{2}}{x}$. Substitute $v=t / x$ : $a=\frac{1-(t / x)^{2}}{x}=\frac{x^{2}-t^{2}}{x^{3}}$. From the original equation, $x^{2}-t^{2}=1$, so $a=\frac{1}{x^{3}}$.

questions.questionText: A person travelling on a straight line moves with a uniform velocity $v_{1}$ for some time and with a uniform velocity $v_{2}$ for the next equal time. The average velocity is $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. If $v_{1}=6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$, then $v_{2}$ is_______     $$\left( {{\text{in}}\,m/s} \right)$$.

solutions.newText:
For equal time intervals, $v_{a v g}=\frac{v_{1}+v_{2}}{2}$.
$$
10=\frac{6+v_{2}}{2} \Longrightarrow 20=6+v_{2} \Longrightarrow v_{2}=14 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
$$

questions.questionText: The position of a particle along the x -axis is given by $x=t^{3}-6 t^{2}+5 t$. The magnitude of velocity of the particle when its acceleration becomes zero is______$\qquad$(in $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$).

solutions.newText: $v=\frac{d x}{d t}=3 t^{2}-12 t+5 . \quad a=\frac{d v}{d t}=6 t-12$. Set $a=0 \Longrightarrow \quad 6 t-12=0 \Longrightarrow t=2 s$. $v(2)=3(2)^{2}-12(2)+5=12-24+5=-7 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$. The magnitude is $|-7|=7 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$.

questions.questionText: A car moving with a speed of $54 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}$ is brought to rest in a distance of 22.5 m . The uniform retardation is________ $$({\text{in}}\quad \;\;\;m/{s^2})$$.

solutions.newText: $u=54 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{h}=15 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} . v=0, s=22.5 \mathrm{~m}$. Using $v^{2}=u^{2}+2 a s \Longrightarrow 0=15^{2}+2 a(22.5) \Longrightarrow 0=225+45$ a. $a=-5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$. Retardation is $5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$.

questions.questionText: A stone is dropped from a tower of height 125 m . The time taken to reach the ground is__________ $$({\text{in}}\quad \;\;\;s)$$. (Use $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$ )

solutions.newText: Using $s=u t+\frac{1}{2} a t^{2}$. $125=0 \cdot t+\frac{1}{2}(10) t^{2} \Longrightarrow 125=5 t^{2} \Longrightarrow t^{2}=25 \Longrightarrow t=5 \mathrm{~s}$.
